entry.title: I built PenDown — a live quiz app named after 'pens down!' Come break it
entry.summary:
Remember when the invigilator shouted "pens down!"? I turned that into a quiz app.
That exact moment — pens hitting the desk at once, everyone caught mid-thought — is the whole idea behind PenDown, a live quiz app I just built and shipped. 🔗 Try it: https://pendown.live Someone hosts a quiz (or just launches the built-in demo — takes 5 seconds) Everyone else joins from their phone with a 6-character code — no signup, no app to install Questions come in live with a countdown When time's up, every screen gets stamped: PEN DOWN!
Live leaderboard after every question, final results at the end It's built for the exact moment you'd actually use it — a college quiz night, a team icebreaker, a family group chat challenge, killing time with friends. I want strangers to break it before real users do. Friends are too nice when they test things. So: Grab a friend, coworker, or literally anyone in a group chat and play a round together (it's way more fun with 2+ people) Try the demo quiz if you just want to poke around solo Tell me what felt off, slow, confusing, or just didn't land Genuinely curious whether the nostalgia hook lands for people who didn't grow up with the same "pens down" moment, too — would love to hear if this feels universal or very specifically an Indian-exam-hall thing. https://pendown.live — go make some noise.

entry.title: Design Tokens as AI Guardrails: Keeping AI-Generated Screens On-Brand
entry.summary: The coding agents got good at layout. Ask Cursor, Claude Code, or Lovable for a pricing card and you get a recognisable, mostly-correct row of features with a button on the bottom — in about three seconds. The thing they're not good at is the part underneath: which blue, how much spacing, which grey for borders, what radius pairs with what shadow. They pick from an infinite palette and they pick badly. A constrained token set is the cheapest, most reliable guardrail you can put in front of that. The surprise isn't that tokens help. The surprise is how aggressively they help the agent — not the human.
